title: Legion
summary: Legion is the dark Legendary Titan of War, whose power allows him to absorb other Titans and use their powers at his own will. Once the Titan of the Betrayer, he was given to Rassimov and hidden deep within his body to be used as his secret weapon.

sections.heading: History
sections.text:
Legion once belonged to the Betrayer and was used to fight against the Casterwill family across many generations. Throughout the ages, Legion absorbed thousands of Titans, including an Icarus and a Feyone Titan. [Rassimov's Secret]

Legion's Amulet was eventually laid to rest in North Africa until the modern age, when it was gifted to Rassimov by the spirit of the Betrayer. [Rassimov's Secret] On the Betrayer's orders, Rassimov stole the Amulet from its resting place in North Africa, while on a covert Organization mission during his time as an undercover agent. He hid the Amulet within his body to avoid detection. [Legion Amulet (GP Card)]

Some months after Rassimov revealed his true allegiance to the Blood Spiral, the Huntik Foundation ambushed him in Egypt, and Dante Vale used Sorrowbond to take all of Rassimov's Titans, unaware that Legion was hidden within Rassimov's body. Upon escaping Foundation arrest, Rassimov then revealed his secret and invoked Legion. After sustaining multiple attacks from Dante, Umbra, Lok Lambert and the Willblade, it quickly became clear that Legion was no normal Titan. After being knocked into the sand by Powerbonded Lindorm, Legion recovered and, to everyone's horror, absorbed Lindorm, destroying his Amulet. He then defeated Powerbonded Kipperin as Lok attempted to invoke Pendragon. Dante attempted to lead Rassimov away with the Necklace of Tutankhamun but this was snatched by Dante's Solwing who sought to allow the team time to escape. Legion then caught up with Solwing and absorbed him, destroying his Amulet much to Dante's sadness. [Rassimov's Secret]

The team were still feeling distressed following Legion's attack whilst recovering at Lok's home in Country Kerry, Ireland. Dante, in particular, was still exhausted from the battle. [Back Home]

Rassimov invoked Legion again at the battle at the Spiral Mark where he fought Lok's Dendras and Sophie's Feyone. He used Lindorm's Spinnerslash ability to attack them. He fought against Powerbonded Baselaird, overpowering and almost absorbing him, forcing Lok to call him back to his Amulet. Legion then partially absorbed Dendras before attempting to absorb Feyone. However, he was defeated by Lok Lambert who used the Willblade to destroy Legion's Amulet, weakened due to holding the energy of thousands of extra Titans absorbed through the years. With Legion's destruction, all of the Titans that he had absorbed over the ages were released back to the Spirit World. [The Spiral Mark]

Legion is a Titan of devastating power. Despite his huge size, he can move extremely fast, sprinting across the battlefield. In combat, he uses his giant fists to punch his enemies or stomp on them with his feet. He is able withstand multiple attacks simultaneously from different angles without so much as weakening. Sophie Casterwill stated that she had never seen a Titan able to endure so much damage all at once. [S2E47] 

Legion's primary and most devastating power his Titan Absorption ability. Once he has grabbed a Titan in his hands, he can absorb them into his body, trapping them inside himself and destroying their Amulet for good. He can then utilize any of the absorbed Titans' abilities against his enemies for himself. When a Titan has been absorbed, its Amulet will completely disintegrate and the Titan's icon will appear on Legion's chest. [Rassimov's Secret] However, storing the energy of thousands of extra Titans also made Legion's Amulet extremely vulnerable as Amulets are only meant to balance the energy of one Titan. Lok was able to destroy it with the Willblade, destroying Legion and releasing all the absorbed Titans to return to the Spirit World. [The Spiral Mark]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.wikitext:
* His summoning command is "'''Unleash'''".
* Legion's name may be derived from a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legion_(demons) group of demons that possessed a man] that Jesus later healed according to the gospels of Mark and Luke in the Christian Bible. His appearance is based on that of [[wikipedia:Frankenstein's monster|Frankestein's monster]].
* Legion, along with [[Overlos]] and [[Pendragon]], is one of the few [[Legendary Titans]] not to be contained in a [[Ring]].
